correctness.rationale: In GP(12,5) the graph built from outer step 1, inner step 5 and the spokes has 24 vertices of degree three. Starting from N[S], unique-neighbor forcing computes a well-defined closure: enlarging the observed set cannot invalidate a force to a vertex still unobserved. Exhaustion of 24 singletons, 276 pairs and 2024 triples gives 0,0,576 successes. On precisely these minimum triples, an exchange generates a jump and an exchange of adjacent vertices generates a slide; the latter always changes the occupancy parity in one part of the bipartite base graph. Independent all-source distance calculations on both graphs cover all 165600 unordered pairs, including the full paired-distance penalty profile. They confirm 6660 and 1152 edges, slide degree four, radius/diameter 4/4 and 9/10, slide eccentricities 432 of nine and 144 of ten, and exactly 396 maximum-penalty pairs split by (slide,jump) lengths (8,1):324 and (10,3):72. In the permutation-star presentation, symbol permutations and permutations of positions 1–3 preserve star edges; the two commuting actions have trivial common kernel since the center of S4 is trivial. The checked explicit adjacency-preserving bijection maps those 144 automorphisms to the GP labels. The orbit computation gives the five stated triple orbits; separate GP automorphism enumeration verifies that the displayed pair generates exactly all 72 diametral pairs and these cover each eccentricity-ten vertex once. Since the displayed subgroup already has 144 elements, the independent group enumeration applies to the stated subgroup too.
residual_risks: The finite exhaustion is exact for this graph and these minimum-set move models, not an extrapolation to generalized Petersen graphs or larger admissible sets.

evidence: Bjorkman et al. define TAR, TJ and TS but describe their power-domination results for TAR/k-TAR and TJ. Anderson and Kuenzel's general cubic bounds do not count the optima or their moves; the sharper claw-free hypothesis fails at u_0. The Petersen-pair classification covers GP(n,2), n>=9, with minimum cardinality two and unrestricted exchange.

originality.rationale: Existing reconfiguration definitions, cubic power-domination bounds, the classical Nauru graph and its symmetry are background. The supported distinct result is the exact minimum-configuration jump and slide metric comparison, in particular the distance-ten orbit and its perfect pairing of the eccentricity-ten configurations. Related results on different cubic graphs share some exact numbers or orbit phenomena but do not give the Nauru values or pair structure.
residual_risks: Unindexed exact computations may exist; focused primary and catalogue checks do not establish uniqueness. The minimum cardinality by itself is not the basis for the originality decision.

value.rationale: This is a natural symmetric cubic benchmark for the difference between unrestricted exchange and graph-local movement at the optimum. The 4-regular slide graph is not vertex-transitive: only one configuration orbit is eccentricity ten, and a unique diametral partner pairs precisely that orbit. Even a single jump sometimes requires eight optimality-preserving slides. The paired metric and symmetry certify these distinct obstructions, rather than just adding another graph's count of optimum triples.
residual_risks: No prediction for general sensor networks or universal penalties is supported; scientific value is as an exact structural benchmark.
